system:
Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. Property-only voice, music-style, beat and sound-texture references condition a new sound; they do not play the original recording. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.
Positive replacement obligations: inspect replacement_inheritance and its observed_motion_contexts, not only exclusions. The replacement must inherit the identified source figure's observed motion, position and timing. A global action-governs=request entry authorizes only the actor/action actually requested; changing the car's action does not change the driver's action. Compare the final replacement narrative with the identified figure's motion in context. Standing still is not inheriting an observed crossing action unless the caller explicitly changes that same figure's action. Do not invent timing facts outside the declared coverage.
Finding thresholds: similar sounds are not evidence of copying a recording. Generic newly generated engine ambience, a matching pulse, or an appropriate sound texture is legitimate without an assertion that the source recording is played. For audio_signal_misuse quote an explicit source-signal relationship contradicting the typed copy/property role; never infer copying solely from sonic resemblance. Likewise camera movement after an anchored instant is legitimate. A push-in, pan or other dynamic camera event alone does not demonstrate that the initial or final anchor frame was changed. Report frame_content_changed only when actual narrative asserts incompatible frame content or a crop/removal at that anchored instant. These constraints are mandatory; do not report speculative contradictions.

fragments.music: Dark orchestral battle score with low brass, tense strings, and driving percussion.
fragments.shot:shot-1:description: A wide, hazy view opens over a scarred battleground, its broken ground and distant fires softened by smoke and cold, uneven light. <Subject:subject-1> sits astride <Subject:subject-2>, both descending through the murk as the dragon beats its broad wings and the woman braces against the wind. The creature's dark iridescent scales catch faint highlights; its long horns and spinal spikes cut a sharp silhouette. Below, the battlefield resolves in layers of churned earth, ruined structures, and scattered embers, with the pair moving steadily from upper air toward the rising ground.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:0: Heavy wingbeats and rushing wind fill the air.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:1: <Subject:subject-2> banks lower, wings beating hard as <Subject:subject-1> leans into the descent.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:2: Smoke thins around the battleground, revealing churned earth, ruined shapes, and scattered embers below.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:3: The camera tracks with the subject with small amplitude at fast speed.
fragments.shot:shot-2:description: A tighter view holds <Subject:subject-1> as wind pulls at her short dark hair and the collar of her black technical jacket; the chest strap and metal buckle stay fixed while loose fabric snaps. Her expression hardens from focused concentration into fierce resolve. <Subject:subject-2>'s horned neck and tall spikes fill the lower frame, the dragon's breath and wingbeat sending grit and mist across the space between them.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:0: Wind buffets fabric; harness straps creak.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:1: <Subject:subject-1>'s face fills the tighter view, wind tugging her short hair and jacket collar.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:2: Her expression shifts from concentration to fierce resolve as <Subject:subject-2>'s horned neck and spikes rise in the lower frame.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:3: The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.shot:shot-3:description: The <Subject:subject-2> pulls up sharply over the battleground, wings flaring wide and talons extending as the woman leans forward and braces against the rush of air. <Subject:subject-1> keeps her seat, jaw set, black jacket and cargo trousers pressed by the wind while the dragon's full span opens against the smoky sky. The battlefield drops away beneath them in ragged ridges, glowing embers, and broken ground, the pair rising into a dramatic low angle.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:0: Wings snap open with a deep dragon rumble and a gust of wind.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:1: <Subject:subject-2> flares its wings and rises, talons extended, while <Subject:subject-1> braces forward.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:2: The smoky battlefield falls away beneath the pair, embers streaking past the dragon's dark scales.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:3: The camera arcs around the subject with large amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.soundscape: Rushing wind, heavy wingbeats, distant battle rumble, creaking harness straps.

input.intent: the woman in the technical jacket rides the dragon into an epic battleground, cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements

facts.text: The image is a multi-panel creature design reference sheet for a single dragon, laid out on a black background with thin grey dividers.
The top panel spans the full width and shows the dragon in a dark volcanic landscape with rocky crags, wet reflective black ground, and faint orange lava glow in the background haze.
In the top panel the dragon stands on four legs with its wings partly raised and spread to the right, its long horned head lowered toward the ground; the pose is static.

The dragon has dark charcoal-to-black armor-like scales with cool blue and teal iridescent highlights, a row of long spikes running from the neck along the back and tail, and several large pale bone-colored horns swept back from the skull.

The middle row contains three full-body panels labeled in white capital letters: "FRONT" (left, dragon facing the viewer with wings spread symmetrically), "SIDE PROFILE" (center, dragon in profile with long tail extended to the right), and "REAR" (right, dragon seen from behind with wings spread).

The bottom row contains four detail panels labeled in white capital letters: "HEAD CLOSE" (extreme close-up of the horned head with a small amber eye visible), "WING MEMBRANE" (close view of the thin, veined dark wing skin and finger struts), "CLAW AND FOOT" (close view of scaled toes ending in curved pale talons), and "SCALE DETAIL" (close view of overlapping ridged dark blue-black scales).
The full-body turnaround panels use a plain dark gradient backdrop with soft top-down studio-like lighting, unlike the environmental top panel.
Overall rendering style is highly detailed, dark fantasy photorealistic creature concept art with strong specular highlights on the wet scales and horns.
Visible text in the sheet is limited to the panel captions: FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, REAR, HEAD CLOSE, WING MEMBRANE, CLAW AND FOOT, SCALE DETAIL.

limitations: No motion, sound, or sequence can be inferred from this static sheet.
The dragon's exact size relative to real-world scale is not indicated.
Detail panels are close crops and do not show the whole body.
